The Reds were involved in a stalemate at the Broadfield Stadium but the Reds did start the brighter of the two sides but failed to test Matthew Cox in the Barnet goal.

Barnet grew into the game and forced Mannone into a couple of saves and they used that momentum into the second dominating the possession and the chance but Crawley were resilient and Mannone denied the Bees a handful of times to extend Crawley’s unbeaten run in the league under Kevin Blackwell.

According to recent reports, vito Mannone - 8.5: The Italian shot stopper pulled off a great stop low down to his left on 25 minutes to keep the score at 0-0. His distribution out to the wide areas was accurate and effective as the Reds were able to win the flick-ons. Made a number of crucial saves in the second half to ultimately claim Crawley a hard fought point.

Kellan Gordon - 7: Delivered a lot of crosses from into the Barnet box and found himself in a lot of space down the right-hand side.

Josh Flint - 6.5: The centre half moved to the right side of the back three and put in a solid shift coming out on top of a lot of his duels.

Pemi Aderoju – 7.5: His hold up play was second to none and was effective at bringing others into the game.

Lewis Richards – 6: Playing in the wing back role, Richards defended well when required and played a number of decent balls into the channel for Orsi to run onto.

Jonny Russell – 6.5: Moving into the back three from wing-back he didn’t look out of place and dealt with Barnet’s number fast and physical nine Jack Maskell extremely well.

Dylan Morgan – 7: Picked up the ball in some great central positions and used his neat footwork to bypass the Barnet players and move the ball into space.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Ibrox manager praised the resilience of his players after they managed to overturn a half-time deficit to beat a revitalised Aberdeen 3-2 in a thrilling contest, courtesy of a decisive ten-minute goal blitz early in the second half.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes has warned his Rangers side they must learn to control games more efficiently for longer periods if they are to sustain their Scottish Premiership title challenge this season.

The Ibrox manager praised the resilience of his players after they managed to overturn a half-time deficit to beat a revitalised Aberdeen 3-2 in a thrilling contest, courtesy of a decisive ten-minute goal blitz early in the second half.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, McInnes was frustrated that Rangers allowed their opponents back swiftly into the contest after establishing a seemingly unassailable cushion, which left them clinging on during an increasingly anxious finale.

Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin turned the game around, before Findlay Marshall's immediate response ensured the Dons went down fighting.

Despite the satisfaction of extending their unbeaten run to 14 matches, McInnes was unhappy with the manner in which his team surrendered control, insisting his players put unnecessary pressure on themselves.

Industry observers note that “Delighted we've got the job done. Great win for us in the end,” he stated. “Disappointed we've allowed ourselves to be hanging on at the end rather than controlling the game. The question was being asked of us at half-time. We were in a difficult spot. We were having to dig it deep and you find out about your players in these sort of situations. It's good to know that we have dug that result out.

“We need to recognise that we need to be better for longer periods, particularly at Ibrox. By conceding the second goal, we should still stay on the job, but with too many negative passes, too many backwards passes, we need to own that a wee bit.

"The biggest takeaway for me tonight is my players had to dig deep. We were in a tough spot at half-time, 50,000, 1-0 down at home to Aberdeen. That's not an easy place to be. It's alright for me to try and address it tactically, having a go at half-time or whatever, but they've still got to go and deliver, and they delivered a big performance.”.

In a recent development, mcInnes had initially opted for a system designed to exploit the spaces around Aberdeen's front two, with Gassama and Badredine Bouanani providing width on both flanks. However, he conceded that his side had not been productive enough despite repeatedly getting into promising positions in the final third before a triple half-time substitution altered the formation to provide greater control in central areas.

“I thought the subs helped us and I thought for 20 minutes we were outstanding,” McInnes added. “We showed the speed, the intensity, the quality, the intelligence. We blew them away.”.

Fresh Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick was left frustrated by his side’s collapse immediately after half-time, but felt they had shown enough to suggest Rangers were there for the taking.

“I am disappointed with the five or six minutes after half-time. That hurts,” he stated. “We saw a good performance, Rangers were beatable tonight. We need more time. We have to improve. We have to talk about those ten minutes.

“After 3-1 down we came back and we believed in ourselves. We deserved the equaliser. We came to win and we are disappointed to go back with zero points. I see a lot of positives things.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The stalemate made it eight points in four games in charge for Blackwell as Reds closed the gap on safety in League Two.

Reds had chances in the first half but second-placed Barnet put on the pressure in the second half but a mixture of solid defending and an inspired Vito Mannone kept the visitors at bay.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

According to recent reports, “Wow, bloody hell, that was tough”, noted Blackwell. "It's a very direct game, that's for sure, and they played it quite well, so I'm really pleased with the way the players dealt with it.

“They're an experienced side and we had a lot of youngsters again today, so all credit to them. "I thought Ben Heneghan, once again, at the centre of the back three has done really well.

“It's a typical system to play against and I can see why they're high up in the league, it's causing teams problems. But I think overall, you know, Vito's not had many saves to make it, has he?.”.

In a recent development, blackwell was pleased with how his reduced the amount of gilt-edged chances Dean Brennan’s side had. “There wasn't clear-cut chances,” he said. “It's a system that I've not seen for a long time, but it just meant we had to be focused all the time, they do things quickly, they're long throws, long balls, the keeper kicks it from box to box.

According to recent reports, “They know that the big nine is going to flick it on and they make runners in behind and your midfield and your centre-halves have to stay with runners. So it was a disciplined performance tonight against a team, like I say, who play a very direct style, but are good at what they do.”.

And the former Leeds boss highlighted that despite the gap in league positions, there was not much in quality between the two sides.

According to recent reports, blackwell said: “You look at it, it was top versus bottom, but you wouldn't have known. I don't think you'd have known.

According to recent reports, “Yes, they put us under a bit of pressure towards the end and exactly what a team at the top, full of confidence, you'd expect them to do that. But we were resilient and it's a difficult one for me to express the game other than it was concentration, do your job, throw your body in the way when required and stand up to a team that can bully you if you allow them to. Like I stated, you know, Pemi [Aderoju] and Osman [Kamara] and Duke [Stephen Duke-McKenna, they've got a lot of youngsters we have and you're going to learn a lot from that.

“I hope they learn a lot. But what I'm pleased about is the resilience.”.

And Blackwell added: “The question was about people coming to Crawley and getting easy points and I think we put a statement down certainly today that if you want to come to Crawley, you're going to have to earn your points if you want to work away with anything.

“So, once again, it's all credit to the players.”.

Tech Report: Kings of the jungle? This early human had surprising survival skills that rivalled ours

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S.
  • Recent findings suggest that homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives.
  • Recent findings suggest that did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Recent findings suggest that homo erectus is already one of humans’ most extraordinary ancient relatives. The big-brained, tool-wielding species emerged two million years ago in Africa and expanded across Eurasia, before vanishing around 100,000 years ago in Java, Indonesia.

Recent findings suggest that did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Industry observers note that did Homo erectus and Denisovans mate? Tooth proteins hint at ancient trysts.

Researchers have now added another feather to the hominin’s cap. A pair of studies analysing fossil teeth1,2, which were published in Nature on 18 November, suggest that H. erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.

Researchers had thought that H. erectus was limited to savannahs and open woodlands, indicates Kira Westaway, a geochronologist at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia, and a co-author of both studies.

In a recent development, “Never, ever have we seen them in rainforests,” she adds. “This is a really big deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Recent findings suggest that the earliest H. erectus fossils, from eastern Africa, are 1.9 million years old. But the svelte, upright-walking and running hominins wasted little time, reaching western Asia and present-day China some 200,000 years later and modern Java, using land bridges, not long after. The last-known H. erectus remains, from central Java, date to roughly 110,000 years ago3.

Limestone caves in Guangxi province, southern China, contained more than 10,000 fossil teeth.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

While looking for fossils from a three-metre-tall great ape called Gigantopithecus, Westaway and her colleagues identified a pair of limestone caves in Guangxi province in southern China. There, they discovered more than 10,000 fossil teeth from animals such as orangutans (Pongo spp.), monkeys and wild boar (Sus spp.), as well as 9 from hominins. The researchers estimate that the hominins lived between 184,000 and 324,000 years ago, according to dating of both fossils and the surrounding sediments using various methods.

Eight of the hominin teeth resembled those of H. erectus in their shape, a designation that was confirmed by analysing the sequences of proteins preserved in the dental enamel of four specimens, states co-author Frido Welker, a molecular palaeoanthropologist at the University of Copenhagen.

The tooth enamel was analysed and its proteins sequenced.Credit: Kira Westaway (Macquarie University).

The ninth lacked the shape and protein signature of H. erectus teeth, states Welker, and it also didn’t resemble those of H. sapiens or Neanderthals (Homo neanderthalensis). Denisovans — enigmatic ancient humans first discovered in southern Siberia and now linked to diverse fossils from China and elsewhere in Asia — are a possibility, but the evidence is circumstantial, says Welker. “Every label we put on that ninth tooth is a little bit of speculation.”.

The multitude of animal teeth was probably accumulated by a scavenger such as a porcupine. The presence of fossils from species such as muntjac deer (Muntiacus muntjac), leopards and orangutans hints at a rainforest environment.

Sources indicate that arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them. At this rate, he might justify his enormous £75m transfer fee by Christmas.

Industry observers note that the Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London. Against Leeds United here, as it was against Sunderland last month, he came off the bench when the champions were struggling. And as it was at Sunderland, he produced a thumping finish to put Arsenal on their way to three points.

This is the value of signing a 28-year-old with significant Premier League experience. As Arsenal laboured against an impressively organised and courageous Leeds side, Mikel Arteta knew that Guimarães was capable of coming into the game and adjusting to its demands. There has been no adaptation period required for Guimarães, who is fast becoming one of the most popular players in north London.

Industry observers note that the finish, which put Arsenal 2-1 ahead at the Emirates Stadium, marked an emphatic conclusion to a fabulous passing sequence. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all combined at speed before Guimarães charged on to Rice’s flick. “It was a beauty,” said Arteta of the goal. The move had actually begun at the feet of Guimarães a few moments earlier, when he nutmegged an opponent in style.

The winning goal came just eight minutes after Riccardo Calafiori, Arsenal’s thrilling left-back/centre-forward hybrid, had pulled them level in the game. James Justin had struck for Leeds shortly after half-time, creating a horrible anxiety among the home fans here, and for much of the afternoon Daniel Farke’s side were the better team.

Sources indicate that leeds, though, could not compete with Arsenal for depth. The arrival of Guimarães as a 63rd-minute substitute represented a flexing of Arteta’s managerial muscle, in his first match since signing a newly introduced long-term contract, and the Brazilian offered a moment of attacking quality that his opponents were unable to replicate.

It has been revealed that it was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

Sources indicate that this gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” noted Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

In a recent development, guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” mentioned Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”.

It has been revealed that leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

According to recent reports, if they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

  • Separated by one point midway through the league phase, Inter Milan and Stuttgart will meet for a Champions League clash at San Siro on Wednesday evening.
  • After contrasting results last time out, Inter trail behind their German visitors, with both sides vying for entry to the knockout round playoffs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 15:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Separated by one point midway through the league phase, Inter Milan and Stuttgart will meet for a Champions League clash at San Siro on Wednesday evening.

After contrasting results last time out, Inter trail behind their German visitors, with both sides vying for entry to the knockout round playoffs.

Having exited at the first knockout stage last season - losing both playoff legs to Bodo/Glimt - Inter started this term's Champions League campaign slowly, taking nothing from their first two fixtures.

The Scudetto holders subsequently bounced back, though, posting consecutive wins without conceding a goal, against Shakhtar Donetsk and Feyenoord.

Shortly before the international break, Inter travelled to De Kuip and left with maximum points, thanks to goals from Yann Bisseck, Francesco Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski.

Such a start sums up their mixed fortunes since being humbled by Paris Saint-Germain in the 2025 final: Cristian Chivu's Champions League record as head coach reads seven wins and seven defeats.

Compared to life under his predecessor Simone Inzaghi, the Nerazzurri have been much less solid at the back, and they shipped yet more goals in a spectacular Serie A contest on Sunday night.

Despite Esposito's hat-trick, Inter ultimately had to settle for a 4-4 draw against local rivals Atalanta, and that left them three points behind surprise league leaders Lazio.

In stark contrast to their Italian counterparts, Stuttgart kicked off the league phase with back-to-back victories, scoring three goals against both Slovan Bratislava and Viking.

Then, they held Atletico Madrid to a 1-1 home draw, before visiting Istanbul to face Turkish champions Galatasaray on matchday four.

Already trailing by two goals inside 15 minutes, the German club never really recovered, suffering their first loss and slipping down to 14th place in the Champions League standings.

Despite holding on to highly-rated coach Sebastian Hoeness, Die Roten have struggled in the Bundesliga this season, losing half of their first 10 games.

While Inter were sharing eight goals in Bergamo, Stuttgart played out a 0-0 draw with Schalke last weekend, leaving them eighth in the table and eight points behind the top four.

Still, the Swabian side have recently improved a once porous defence, posting three clean sheets from four domestic matches before heading to Milan.

Stuttgart Champions League form:.

Stuttgart form (all competitions):.

Although Inter threw away two points against Atalanta, they were able to welcome back their inspirational captain, as Lautaro Martinez made his return from injury with a late cameo.

Having conceded a stoppage-time penalty against his former club, Alessandro Bastoni will hope to fare better on Wednesday, when he returns from a Champions League suspension.

Benjamin Pavard made 88 appearances for Stuttgart between 2016 and 2019, and the Frenchman may join Bastoni in a three-man defence.

The hosts will be missing key midfielder and set-piece specialist Hakan Calhanoglu due to a thigh injury, while Ange Bonny is also ruled out.

Martinez must vie with Marcus Thuram and Manchester United target Esposito to feature up front, but there is no doubt about Stuttgart's star striker.

Ermedin Demirovic has already netted a club-record four goals in this season's Champions League campaign, added to five in the Bundesliga.

By contrast, Deniz Undav has yet to score in the German top flight, but he is still set to support Demirovic at San Siro.

Though Hoeness has most of his squad available, Luca Jaquez (rib), Leo Sauer (muscular) and Angelo Stiller (groin) are presently injured.

Inter Milan possible starting lineup:.

J. Martinez; Pavard, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Zielinski, Sucic, Dimarco; Esposito, L. Martinez.

Stuttgart possible starting lineup:.

Bredlow; Hendriks, Chabot, Mittelstadt; Leweling, Karazor, Promel, Fuhrich; Undav, El Khannouss; Demirovic.

It's either hit or miss for Inter, who have drawn none of their last 16 Champions League matches, and the Serie A champions will extend that trend with a home win.

Half of their goals in the league phase have arrived inside the final 15 minutes, so Stuttgart may be caught out in the closing stages.

Sixth-placed City, who drew 2-2 with struggling Doncaster Rovers at the weekend, face another White Rose side who have had a difficult autumn in the Reds, who find themselves at the bottom of League One following Bromley's weekend win at Reading.

Without a win in 10 league games since September 2 and in their worst league position for many a year, the Oakwell outfit look like being in the thick of a survival fight for the rest of the season and face the very real prospect of fourth-tier football next term for the first time since 1978-79 if their fortunes don't turn around in the newly introduced year.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It's a far cry from their highs in their one season under Duff in 2022-23 when they reached the play-off final and went desperately close to promotion back to the Championship.

Duff, who was at Oakwell to watch his old club take on Sheffield Wednesday on Friday - the hosts lost 2-1, the margin of defeat for their past five league losses - said: "Barnsley didn't look like a wounded animal on Friday, but a football team with loads of energy and good players.

Industry observers note that "I don't think we're at a point now where we can assume that, well: 'we're just better than them'. Everything that's got us, this football club, the team, the squad, to where it has and the success it's had, is because it's had that underdog mentality. What we can't have is we slip into 'oh, we're better than them'.. Because that's when trouble starts, isn't it?

"I watched them on Friday against Sheffield Wednesday and they should have got some out of the game.

"Barnsley found themselves 2-0 down and then were really, really good for the rest of the game.

"It's not like the Premier League where you very rarely see teams at the bottom of the league beat the teams at the top. In this league, it happens all the time.

Recent findings suggest that “Bromley have beaten Reading, Peterborough have beaten Plymouth. It's not a league where you (think) we’ll beat them or ‘two home games, we’ll win them’.

According to recent reports, "Our lads' mentality and attitude is pretty good. I don't think we have that sort of arrogance in terms of ‘we'll be alright, we'll just win today.’.

"They know what they have to do, they know the effort they have to put in, the application, the energy they have to put into every game and since I've been here they've done that every game.

According to recent reports, "They did it before we came and, like I stated, they just nicked a couple early in the season. We've done enough where we should have won them and we haven't quite nicked them.".

City are on a run of nine matches in just under a month in four different competitions and they face midweek games for the next four matches. Tonight is also their final game of a six-match run of fixtures at Valley Parade.

Duff continued: "There are games that are coming now.

"There’s no way there is going to be the same 11 players on Tuesday or the following Saturday or the following Tuesday or the following Saturday.

"We’ll wrap a few up that we need to and there will be opportunities for people.

"The good thing with competition is they know they’ll get opportunities so they need to be ready. If you get given a chance and you don’t take it, it might not come around again so quickly.

"That’s when the training of the lads who aren’t in the team is so crucial, the lifestyle, the commitment to the job, the commitment to the team.

"Don’t be the one that’s caught out partying or eating junk food because you’re not letting yourself down, you’re letting your teammates down. But I don’t think we need to worry about any of that in this group.".

The dismissal proved costly for Fabian Hurzeler's second placed side, who conceded twice in stoppage time through Oli McBurnie.

However, Costinha will escape a European suspension because his red card was received in a domestic competition.

Under FA rules, receiving a second caution in the same match carries an automatic one-game suspension, which only kicks in for the domestic league and domestic cups.

That means Costinha will miss this Sunday’s match Premier League clash against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium but should be available for Albion’s trip to Bournemouth on December 2.

Uefa operates separately to the Premier League which means Costinha can feature against Universitatea Craiova at the Amex Stadium on Thursday.

Hurzeler admitted the sending-off had a significant impact on Brighton's defeat but insisted the referee was not responsible for the result.

"Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role," he mentioned.

The German added: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards.

"In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going.".

Hurzeler also refused to blame referee Peter Bankes, saying: "The referee wasn't the reason why we lost.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

"I suppose that the hard bit at the minute is we would like to defend as a four, but with Sil (Swinkels) as a left-sided centre-back, he's not as comfortable as we'd like him to be in a left-back position. That's natural.

"Jammer probably has to do a little bit more defensively than we'd like but that's something that we've got to put up with at the minute.

"That's not going to change in the short-term so we've got to make sure we improve and keep working at it.".

Minimising it is partly down to those inside of him.

According to recent reports, "We want him as high up the pitch as possible for as long as possible," explained Challinor. "For that to be the case we need to control the ball.

In a recent development, "If we haven't got the ball, then we have to defend and we end up closer to our goal. If we can look after the ball better and spend more time in the opposition half, he should be in and around the opposition penalty area most of the time.

"That comes down to what we do behind the ball to make sure that's the case.".

It has been revealed that challinor has fielded the same XI in his two league games in charge, both won. But whereas against Plymouth Argyle his side was more often in a 3-2-4-1 which at times became a 4-2-3-1, at Barnsley the emphasis was more the other way around.

Although he picks from the same squad at Broadhall Way, the manager hinted there may be changes.

In a recent development, "It'll be the same group," he noted. "Three younger lads didn't travel on Friday – Jarv (Jarvis Thornton), Gabe (Otegbayo), and Ernie (Weaver). Sean (Fusire)was with us.

In a recent development, "Do we need to freshen up a little bit? We'll look at that and see how the players recover.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 16:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.
  • Stade Pierre-Mauroy will stage a gameweek five Champions League fixture between hosts Lille and six-time European winners Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.
  • The only previous two meetings between these teams came in the 2012-13 group stage when the German giants won both home and away by an aggregate score of 7-1 (1-0 away, 6-1 at home).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 16:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Stade Pierre-Mauroy will stage a gameweek five Champions League fixture between hosts Lille and six-time European winners Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

The only previous two meetings between these teams came in the 2012-13 group stage when the German giants won both home and away by an aggregate score of 7-1 (1-0 away, 6-1 at home).

Lille are one of only three teams out of 36 in this season’s Champions League who enter the halfway stage of the League Phase without a single win to their name, drawing one and losing three of their first four matches, while they are one of 12 teams to have conceded at least 10 goals.

Les Dogues were beaten by Real Betis (3-2), Arsenal (3-0) and Galatasaray (4-2) before playing out a goalless stalemate with Bodo/Glimt in Norway on matchday four, leaving them sitting second-bottom in the 36-team standings and three points behind the playoff positions.

Head coach Davide Ancelotti – the son of five-time UCL winner and ex-Bayern boss Carlo Ancelotti – has seen his Lille side fare better in Ligue 1 this term, as they sit third in the table with 21 points after 11 matches (W6 D3 L2), five points adrift of leaders PSG.

In a recent development, however, Lille head into Wednesday’s contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home defeat to fourth-placed Lyon last weekend. Les Dogues failed to score on the domestic front for the first time this season, with Ancelotti admitting that playing with a false nine ultimately led to a lack of presence in the penalty box.

Lille have been prolific on home soil in the Champions League, though, scoring in each of their last nine such matches, while they have also found the net in each of their last four UEFA encounters against German opposition.

Although Bayern Munich are one of only four teams yet to lose in this season’s Champions League, they currently sit down in 13th place in the League Phase standings after winning two and drawing two of their first four fixtures.

In a recent development, A thumping 5-0 victory over Bodo/Glimt on matchday one was followed by two action-packed draws with Viking FK (3-3) and Arsenal (2-2), conceding late goals in both games. However, the Bavarian giants returned to winning ways with a 2-0 away success over Atletico Madrid three weeks ago.

Supporters have certainly not been short of entertainment when watching Bayern, as they have now scored at least twice in 12 of their last 13 Champions League games, while their last 10 matches in the competition have produced a whopping 50 goals.

Industry observers note that after missing five games following a recent health scare, head coach Vincent Kompany made a welcome return to the touchline with his left arm in a sling for Bayern’s Bundesliga clash at home to Koln last Friday. However, his side were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw, surrendering top spot to Borussia Dortmund who now sit two points clear.

Bayern will be keen to make a swift return to winning ways as they endeavour to climb back into the top-eight of the UCL League Phase, and they should be confident of success on Wednesday having won seven of their last 10 European away matches against French opposition.

Bayern Munich Champions League form:.

Bayern Munich form (all competitions):.

Lille are still having to cope without Tiago Santos and Hamza Igamane who are recovering from long-term knee injuries, but Ethan Mbappe is available to return from a three-match UCL suspension and is set to rival Dilane Bakwa for a start on the right flank.

After returning to training and then featuring as a substitute against Lyon, Ayase Ueda may be in contention to start up front after recovering from a foot injury, while 40-year-old Olivier Giroud is also a natural centre-forward option at Ancelotti’s disposal.

Tanguy Nianzou, who made four UCL appearances for Bayern in the 2021-22 campaign, is likely to start at the heart of the defence alongside Alexsandro, while Nabil Bentaleb, Ngal'ayel Mukau and Benjamin Andre are all set to play in midfield.

Recent findings suggest that as for Bayern, they suffered a major injury blow last Friday as 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane suffered a torn syndesmosis ligament which required surgery. The striker is now expected to be sidelined for at least a few months.

Manuel Neuer (foot), Alphonso Davies (knee/muscle), Serge Gnabry (hamstring) and Ismael Saibari (ankle) are also in the treatment room, while Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Michael Olise (foot) are both doubtful, the latter of whom was seen on crutches and wearing a protective boot after the draw with Koln.

In the absence of Kane, the likes of Diaz - if fit - Jamal Musiala, Noah Codjo-Evora, 17, and Bastian Assomo, 16, are potential candidates to lead the line for Bayern.

Lennart Karl is another attacking option at Kompany’s disposal. At the age of 18 years and 276 days, he has scored five UCL goals, the fourth-most by any player before turning 19. A goal on Wednesday would see him equal Raul in third place, behind Lamine Yamal (11) and Kylian Mbappe (10).

Lille possible starting lineup:.

Ozer; Ngoy, Nianzou, Alexsandro, Perraud; Bentaleb, Andre, Mukau; E. Mbappe, Giroud, Diaoune.

Bayern Munich possible starting lineup:.

Urbig; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanisic; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Boey, Musiala, Brown; Karl.

Lille can feel quietly optimistic about claiming a positive result on home soil against a weakened Bayern side dealing with a mounting injury crisis, particularly with the absence of talisman Kane representing a major blow to the visitors' frontline.

However, even if Kompany is forced to field a makeshift attack, the Bavarian giants still possess enough overall quality and have our backing to edge a closely-fought contest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whereas the Bantams’ squad is built around players who have been around the block, Barnsley's is the complete opposite.

Kelly, one of eight starters below the age of 23, wore the captain's armband in Friday's 2-1 defeat at Sheffield Wednesday, although 31-year-old midfielder Cameron McGeehan is almost certain to return from suspension at Valley Parade.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The callowness of the Reds has been exposed at times this season but as part of a young Northern Ireland team which has had an exceptional start to the season, winning promotion to the top division of the Nations League, Kelly is loathe to use that as an excuse.

"The Northern Ireland team is young, but it's a really experienced team," stressed former Doncaster Rovers player Kelly. "I think if you look at the amount of caps some of the lads have, the Charles brothers (former Sheffield Wednesday players Shea and Pierce) are 23 and 21, but they've played (a combined 57) international games.

"Here it's a lot of lads' first seasons in the EFL, which is completely different.

"But I think young players are fearless and we probably do need to stop looking at us as a young team.

Industry observers note that "I don't actually think that's the reason why we're losing so many games. It's nothing to do with that, I think.".

Whilst the age of the squad probably is a bigger factor than Kelly will admit, he is right that there is no point falling back on it as that will not change this side of the January transfer window at the very earliest.

What Barnsley’s strategy is meant to do is accelerate the development of young players, and Kelly feels wearing the captain's armband – or even taking on more responsibility when others do – is enhancing his game.

According to recent reports, "I really enjoy it," he remarked. "It was a bit different for me coming back this season. From the very start, it was just a lot of a younger changing room.

"I felt really older when I came back compared to when I joined here last year. But it'll be really good for me in the future. I'm quite enjoying it.

According to recent reports, "I'm looking up to Carm a lot, the captain of the group. I speak with him nearly every day. He's really helping me.".

But the focus just has to be on securing a first win in 11 league games.

It has been revealed that "We've got a chance to try and bounce back," stated Kelly. "We need to start winning games, so hopefully start on Tuesday.

"It will be another significant crowd, with a good atmosphere.

In a recent development, "It just makes everyone play another five to ten per cent better, run a bit more when there's a significant crowd. I think the big atmospheres do help.

"Hopefully, it'll help us track a win on Tuesday.".

Daniel Stendel has a decision to make at right-back after Jubril Okedina – a central defender playing out of position there – was culpable for goals in the last two matches.

In a recent development, “It’s a little bit like our performance," mentioned the coach. "We played well but in little moments we are not ready and conceded the goal. He is similar.

Recent findings suggest that "It was not only his fault but he was the last player and maybe he can defend this ball better. It was team mistakes.

“We have the chance to do it better at Bradford and we have some ideas to change some things in the first 11, maybe not.”.

After four games out of the XI, Tyrese Noslin is an option.

Sources indicate that "I think a little bit in the first games it’s not his quality in possession that he has to improve, it’s more his physical game out of possession," said Stendel. "He tried to adapt his game so much more in training every week.

"I hope maybe on Tuesday or maybe Saturday he is ready to start and show he does the next step in his career.".

Striker Tobi Adeyemo is not expected to feature again in 2026, but on-loan winger Amani Richards has an outside chance of playing before Christmas.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 23 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:37.
  • Matchday 17 of the 2026-27 Championship season sees struggling Bristol City host high-flying Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday evening.
  • The home side enter the clash on a run of three consecutive defeats, while Wrexham arrive unbeaten in their last three matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 23 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:37.

Matchday 17 of the 2026-27 Championship season sees struggling Bristol City host high-flying Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday evening.

The home side enter the clash on a run of three consecutive defeats, while Wrexham arrive unbeaten in their last three matches.

Having guided Lincoln City to last season’s League One title with a remarkable 101 points, 12 clear of Cardiff City, Michael Skubala arrived at Bristol City full of confidence, but his start to life at Ashton Gate has been far from ideal.

Saturday’s 2-0 loss to Middlesbrough was an improvement on the 5-0 thrashing by Norwich City a fortnight earlier. Still, it was another disappointing result for the Robins, who have now won just one of their last eight league matches since returning from the September international break (D2, L5).

According to recent reports, with his side currently 18th in the Championship table, Skubala’s quest for back-to-back promotions has become increasingly challenging. However, the 44-year-old oversaw a 28-game unbeaten run last season to secure Lincoln the title and now hopes to engineer a similar turnaround at Bristol City.

Unbeaten in 12 of the last 13 meetings between the sides, Bristol City have enjoyed the upper hand in this fixture as Skubala aims to get the better of his opposite number for the first time in three managerial encounters, having lost the previous two by a combined score of 3-0.

It has been revealed that after the Wrexham clash, Tuesday’s hosts face three promotion hopefuls - West Brom, Swansea City, and West Ham United - over the next four gameweeks. They will need to raise their level to avoid anxiously looking over their shoulder at the bottom three as the hectic festive period approaches.

Wrexham narrowly missed out on a playoff spot last season and were tipped as promotion contenders this term, but after securing just three wins from their opening 13 matches, those expectations were quickly dampened.

Off the back of consecutive defeats to Blackburn Rovers and Sheffield United to close out October, Phil Parkinson’s men have started November with wins over Middlesbrough and, most recently, Lincoln - either side of a 1-1 draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers.

The Red Dragons’ tally of seven points from the last nine available is the joint third-best in the Championship, so they should travel to a ground where they have never previously won in confident mood.

With just six goals in their eight away league matches so far, Wrexham could do with greater attacking impetus as they seek back-to-back victories on the road for the first time since a four-match winning run at the start of January.

Having conceded 30% of their 20 goals in the final 15 minutes of matches, Tuesday’s visitors must address their late-game struggles, particularly against opponents who have scored nearly half of their 16 goals in that period.

Bristol City Championship form:.

Twenty-four-year-old Noah Eile has not featured since September 18 and remains Bristol City’s only fitness concern ahead of Tuesday’s game.

Scott Twine, who has scored four of the hosts’ last seven goals, is expected to return to the starting lineup after being limited to a 30-minute cameo against Middlesbrough last time out.

Liberato Cacace (calf) and Sam Smith (knee) are confirmed absentees for Wrexham, with Cacace still awaiting his first appearance of the 2026-27 season.

Nathan Broadhead (thigh), Seb Revan (hamstring), and Josh Windass (ankle) are major doubts for the visitors, who are also monitoring the fitness of Callum O’Hare.

Kieffer Moore remains his side’s leading scorer with five goals, but has failed to find the net in his last five appearances.

Bristol City possible starting lineup:.

Collins; Pring, Atkinson, Dickie, Tanner; Randell, Kinght; Twine, De Keersmaecker, Cardines; Tolaj.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Doyle, Worrall, Cleworth; Ekomie, Whiteman, Sheaf, Kabore; Thomason, O’Brien; Moore.

Wrexham are the more confident of the two teams, and while Bristol City have struggled to make home advantage count lately, losing four in a row at Ashton Gate, they cannot be counted out.

We anticipate an open, end-to-end contest, with the hosts narrowly emerging victorious to relieve some of the pressure on Skubala.

Industry News: Lionel Messi escapes red card after hurling ball into rival's face in brutal Inter Miami playoff loss

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.
  • In the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 03:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.

In the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia. The deficit was then compounded when Miami fullback Gonzalo Lujan was sent off with a second yellow card.

On the stroke of halftime, Messi nearly joined his teammate in the locker room with a moment of madness on a throw-in.

Tapia and Messi were both standing out of bounds as the Chilean striker prevented the World Cup winner from taking his throw right away.

Messi then used the ball to shove Tapia's face back. When the Columbus man tried jumping in the air to block the throw, Messi then threw the ball into Tapia's head.

Tapia crumbled to the ground as Messi raised his hands asking for a foul on the Crew star.

Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe.

Lionel Messi nearly got sent off during his team's MLS Cup Playoff match against Columbus.

A frustrated Messi launched the ball off the face of Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia as he prevented the Argentina star from taking a quick throw in. Both players received yellow cards.

Tapia got revenge by scoring a brace to lead the Crew to a 3-0 victory on Saturday evening.

Referee Allen Chapman was not happy with either player's antics, showing yellow cards to both Tapia and Messi.

But ultimately, Columbus and Tapia would get the last laugh as they won 3-0 in the best-of-three Round of 16.

Midfielder Taha Habroune scored the second goal of the evening in the 52nd minute as Tapia secured a brace just six minutes later.

The result has Inter Miami on the brink of elimination from the playoffs after winning the title last season. Columbus dominated every facet of the game, thanks in part to owning 62 percent of possession.

Messi attempted two shots on the evening – counting for half of the saves from Crew keeper Patrick Schulte.

Inter Miami must win the next match in Ohio to stay in the playoffs. If the game finishes tied, the rules dictate the match will proceed directly to penalty kicks.

Out of his three prior seasons in the United States, Messi's 2025 MLS Cup victory was an outlier. Miami missed the playoffs in 2023 and were eliminated in the first round in 2024.

Tech Report: Paris Saint-Germain vs Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.
  • Double Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain will look to continue their stroll through this season's league phase, when they welcome Roma to Parc des Princes on Wednesday evening.
  • The competition's top scorers, peerless PSG have claimed maximum points, while their Italian visitors have spectacularly thrown several away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 23 Nov 2026 17:21, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:43.

Double Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain will look to continue their stroll through this season's league phase, when they welcome Roma to Parc des Princes on Wednesday evening.

The competition's top scorers, peerless PSG have claimed maximum points, while their Italian visitors have spectacularly thrown several away.

Having kicked off their second title defence with an emphatic 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava, PSG then posted consecutive 4-2 victories against Manchester City and Barcelona.

Usually sluggish starters in the league phase, Luis Enrique's men then stepped up another gear by smashing six past Villarreal without reply, ruthlessly maintaining their perfect record.

Already out of sight within 16 minutes and two seconds, PSG set a upcoming fastest time to score four goals in a Champions League match, before slightly easing off the gas.

Furthermore, a tally of 20 goals is the most by any club from their first four group or league phase fixtures, and Barca's overall best of 28 is now under serious threat.

Also unbeaten in 14 games at Europe's elite level, Les Parisiens can surpass Lyon's French record by at least avoiding defeat in midweek.

Despite losing Desire Doue to a serious injury, PSG still beat Nice 3-2 on Saturday night, recording their 12th consecutive win across all competitions.

Now leading city rivals Paris FC by three points at the top of the Ligue 1 table, they are well set to sweep all before them again.

Ahead of their first competitive meeting with PSG - a prospect to be feared and savoured in equal measure - Roma warmed up with a 5-1 win over Parma at the weekend.

Staying within two points of surprise Serie A leaders Lazio - their loathed city rivals - the Giallorossi inched ahead of Scudetto holders Inter Milan, largely thanks to a four-goal haul for Donyell Malen.

After another stellar display at Stadio Tardini, Malen has racked up 26 league goals in 2026, while Roma have already fired home 36 this season.

That is more than any other team at this stage of an Italian top-flight campaign since 1950, and Gian Piero Gasperini's side also remain unbeaten.

However, in the Champions League they have effectively let eight points slip, following a late collapse at home to Real Madrid and their big blow-up at Old Trafford earlier this month.

Roma somehow squandered a two-goal lead to lose against Manchester United on matchday four, leaving them 20th in the Champions League standings and at risk of early elimination.

Now bound for France to face the toughest test of all, the Giallorossi have won just one of their last 11 away games in UEFA's top competition, while conceding in all of the last 33.

Paris Saint-Germain Champions League form:.

Paris Saint-Germain form (all competitions):.

Further diminishing PSG's talented front line, Doue must join Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the long road to recovery from an ACL injury.

More positively for Luis Enrique - a former Roma coach - Ousmane Dembele recently made his comeback from a layoff.

Fabian Ruiz has posted goal involvements in all of his last four Champions League appearances, scoring in the last two, and he should start in central midfield.

Club captain Marquinhos moved to Paris from Roma in 2013, while reserve left-back Lucas Digne spent the 2015-16 campaign on loan with the Giallorossi.

Roma welcomed back Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar during the international break, but Lorenzo Pellegrini is still unavailable.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Leonardo Balerdi (ankle) are both struggling to recover in time for Wednesday's game.

Brazilian wing-back Wesley notched a hat-trick of assists in Parma, despite only appearing as a second-half substitute, so he will expect to play at Parc des Princes.

A sure starter up front, Malen now tops the Capocannoniere rankings with 12 Serie A goals, having recently scored in the Nations League and found the net in three consecutive Champions League matches.

Paris Saint-Germain possible starting lineup:.

Safonov; Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes; Zaire-Emery, Vitinha, Ruiz; Akliouche, Dembele, Mayulu.

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.

PSG's latest injury setback will surely have an impact, but the goals and points should keep flowing on Wednesday.

While Gasperini's Roma are often a delight to behold, their defence can be caught out at the very top level, so they will leave Paris empty-handed.

Sheffield United have been urged to “show ambition” and retain Sydie Peck by former Blades star Brian Deane.

The 22-year-old midfielder is going from strength to strength at Bramall Lane and scored his fifth goal of the season in the 4-0 demolition of Watford at the weekend.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has repeatedly been linked with Premier League clubs and a recent report credited the likes of Newcastle United and Sunderland with interest.

Deane, who made 171 appearances across three spells at Bramall Lane, does not want to see Peck depart.

According to recent reports, he told The Yorkshire Post via BetWright.com: “I'd be very surprised if he left. The club has had a really turbulent time in the transfer market in the summer. Obviously, with no parachute payments coming in now, you have to think, what signal does that send to the fans, to the club and to everybody else in the division?

Recent findings suggest that “They have to show some ambition. I think, from the manager's point of view, it'd be a devastating blow if the club were in a position or wanted to be in a position to sell him. The other thing is, from the kid's development, I think it's very crucial to solidify himself at the level and then look to use that as a foundation.

“If he is going to end up in the Premier League, you have to have a ground in somewhere. Sheffield United is, for me, one of the best clubs in the Championship at the moment, he probably couldn't wish to be at a better club.”.

Sheffield United would like to tie Peck down to a new contract, although it may prove difficult to retain the England youth international if the vultures circle.

In a recent interview, Blades boss Chris Wilder mentioned: “We talked about extending the contracts of the young players and Sydie's one of those players that we'd love to have that discussion with.

In a recent development, “If anything comes up that you can't turn down, I don't think anybody would turn that down. I've said it all along, you're not just turning that from a club's point of view, you're turning that down from an opportunity for the player to go and play in the Premier League. I'm glad [about] that because that weren't happening about 15 months ago, the value of the players was zero.”.

Nico Elvedi has cited Daniel Farke as a key influence behind his decision to join Leeds United from Borussia Mönchengladbach.

The 30-year-old spent over a decade at Mönchengladbach and crossed paths with Farke when the Leeds boss spent the 2022/23 season at the Borussia-Park helm.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Following persistent speculation, the pair were reunited at Elland Road in the most recent summer transfer window.

Elvedi has slotted seamlessly into the Leeds defence, most recently pairing up with Tarik Muharemović and James Justin.

In a recent development, opening up on his decision to link up with the Whites on The Official Leeds United Podcast, Elvedi said: “Years ago, Farke was my old coach in Gladbach. It was also a reason I came here.

According to recent reports, “I talked to him before the transfer. I like him as a coach and as person. He’s a massive reason I came here. I just love the club. It’s a lot of tradition and they are starting to build something and I’m just happy to be here.”.

When asked about Farke’s style and whether it had changed, Elvedi stated: “I think it’s similar to Gladbach. Now you have better players and everything, it’s more successful, his style of play, in the Premier League.

“In Germany, it was a little bit difficult for him in Gladbach, just one year there. But here, he did a really good job.”.

An experienced centre-back, Elvedi boasts 79 Switzerland caps as well as a wealth of Bundesliga experience and believes his time spent on the international scene has given him the confidence to perform in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that he said: “It helps me a lot. Also, the World Cup that I played, I’ve seen that I can play on this level and also when I move to Leeds, I know I can play in a Premier League club and can play against the biggest clubs and biggest players in the world. It’s always fun to play and I love it here in the Premier League.”.

At times, the veteran manager cut an exasperated figure answering questions before Tuesday's Championship match at home to Southampton, especially those around the compatibility of academy graduates Arblaster and Peck in midfield.

Arblaster was first to establish himself, and his November 2024 anterior cruciate ligament injury gave Peck the chance to do the same, but the former’s recovery has made opportunities to play together rare.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Saturday was only the fourth time both have started together this season, and the first on the winning team, 4-0 at home to Watrford.

Last season they started together six times, beating Derby County and Oxford United, but losing to Southampton, Middlesbrough, twice, and Preston North End.

That does not take into account that sometimes, such as at home to Wolverhampton Wanderers, Arblaster played further forward.

"Why?" was Wilder’s frustrated response when the question came up.

"Five or six games they've played together.

"We lost at Southampton last season – that's all on Blaster and Peck when we lost 1-0 and missed four golden opportunities in the last ten minutes to get a point at a really good team that was up and running?

"We lost against Preston North End when two centre-halves defended terribly for the goals.

"Sydie came into the team because Blaster got an ACL. Blaster's working his way back.

Sources indicate that "I thought he was outstanding on Saturday and I thought so was Sydie. Two young academy players playing in a Championship team as a pair.

"It's absolute nonsense. Complete nonsense.

"If I didn't think they could play together, I wouldn't pick them.".

With former Leeds United player Kalvin Phillips due back from an adductor injury, Wilder believes whatever combination of midfielders he picks can work together.

"They've all got different attributes," he argued. "We don't go with a six (holder) and an eight (box-to-box player).

"Jairo (Riedewald) possibly is better a little bit deeper, Kalvin can play higher up, Joe Rothwell can. He can dictate the game as well.

"We've got a lovely combination of young and experienced players.".

"Do you know what does my head in? People waiting for them to fail.

"I can't get my head around that – that people out there are waiting for Blaster and Sydie not to play well.

"They're two young players, two Sheffield United players, one (Arblaster) a Sheffield boy and one absolutely ingrained and gets what it's like to play for Sheffield United, an England Under-21 international. Blaster has come right the way through the England process too.".

At times Wilder's words were reminiscent of ex-Bradford City manager Gary Bowyer's recent comments about unqualified people expressing opinions on football that they would never do to a car mechanic about how they were fixing their car.

Recent findings suggest that "At times, I just want to scream out and say a few more words than I do," admitted Wilder. "Have a bit of belief, have a bit of trust in what we're trying to do.

It has been revealed that "Have a little bit of context. Have a little bit of patience with where we are at the moment.

It has been revealed that "He (Burton manager Bowyer) has been possibly a little bit braver than I am. That might have came out from me a few years ago but I'm a little bit calmer now.

"It's opinions, it's things that you talk about, it keeps the game alive.

"The Peck-Blaster one, I disagree.".

Sources indicate that wilder is annoyed he will be without Japhet Tanganga against Southampton after the captain’s fifth yellow card of the season on Saturday. He believes Tanganga needs to be more "streetwise", and that refereeing and suspension punishments should be more sympathetic.

"I'm disappointed for the skipper to miss out," he said.

"(There was a booking)j after (two minutes) and then quite frequently right the way through the game (13 across the two teams).

According to recent reports, "One of the favourite ones from Pro Ref, as it's now called, is that not every challenge is a yellow card. Well, it seemed to be on Saturday. It wasn't a feisty game.".

Tanaganga was booked late on after a tackle in the middle of the field.

"I've said to Japh, you have to be a bit more streetwise in that moment," said Wilder. "Four-nil going into the 87th minute and knowing how the game has been played with the amount of yellow cards there are.

"But there's got to be some sort of creative way that we can deal with the suspension because we want all our players available.

"To get through to 19 games without picking up five yellows is ridiculous if that's going to be the decision-making.".

Ben Brereton Diaz is unavailable against the club he is on loan from.

  • Two teams that have struggled during the league stage of the 2026-27 Champions League will lock horns on Wednesday, as Slavia Prague welcome Villarreal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 17:36, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:42.

Two teams that have struggled during the league stage of the 2026-27 Champions League will lock horns on Wednesday, as Slavia Prague welcome Villarreal.

The two sides previously went to battle in the 2017-18 Europa League group stage, with the corresponding clash in that campaign finishing 2-0 to Villarreal.

Slavia Prague boast a record of zero wins, one draw and three defeats from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League, with one point leaving them down in 34th spot in the table.

The Red and Whites opened their Champions League league stage campaign with a 3-2 defeat to Lens, before going down 2-0 to Sabah, but they managed to pick up their first point on October 20, drawing 2-2 with Fenerbahce.

Jindrich Trpisovsky's side can also take plenty of positives from their performance against Arsenal in the competition last time out, going down 2-1 to the Gunners.

Slavia Prague will enter this match off the back of successive league wins over Artis Brno and Sigma Olomouc, with the results leaving them top of their domestic table, boasting 37 points from their first 15 games of the campaign.

The Red and Whites have only been victorious in one of their previous 13 matches against Spanish opposition, losing six times in the process, and they have never actually managed to beat a Spanish club in the Champions League proper.

Villarreal, meanwhile, are unbeaten in their nine previous matches against Czech clubs, recording six wins in the process; the Yellow Submarine have also been victorious in three of their five games in Czechia, including the last two.

The La Liga club finished 35th in last season's league stage, so there is huge room for improvement this term, but it has been another difficult European campaign to date.

Inigo Perez's side opened their league stage campaign with a 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund, before recording a 3-1 win over Napoli, but they have lost their last two in the competition against Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain.

Villarreal have three points from their four matches in this season's league stage, which has left them down in 28th spot in the table.

The Yellow Submarine will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 defeat to Barcelona, with the result leaving them 10th in the La Liga table.

Slavia Prague will be without the services of Stepan Chaloupek (hamstring), David Moses (muscular), Adonija Ouanda (muscular), Elias Pitak (ankle) and Danijel Sturm (muscular) due to injury problems.

Meanwhile, Lukas Provod (tendon) needs to be assessed before a final decision is made on his involvement in the Champions League fixture.

Wiktor Nowak and Mojmir Chytil have netted seven times each for Slavia Prague this season, and the pair are both expected to be in the starting side.

As for Villarreal, Ilias Akhomach (muscular), Alassane Diatta (hamstring), Juan Foyth (muscular) and Gerard Moreno (muscular) are absent due to injury problems.

Georges Mikautadze has scored five goals and registered two assists in 18 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season, and the 26-year-old will feature in the final third.

There is also expected to be a spot in the starting side for Tani Oluwaseyi, who has four goals and one assist in 13 appearances during the current campaign.

Markovic; Holes, Zima, N’Guessan; Vlcek, Sadilek, Nowak, Jurasek; Ayaosi, Suleiman; Chytil.

Villarreal possible starting lineup:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it is one etched into Barnsley folklore. Bradford City were famously the opposition as the Reds provided one of those wonderful, soul-enhancing moments that lights up football from time to time as they reached the top-flight for the first occasion in their history.

At the minute, Barnsley supporters have only memories to cling onto. It’s pretty grim in the present - with just over a month to go, 2026 has already marked itself out as one of the most inauspicious in the Reds’ modern-day history.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that how they needed something on a cold, dank West Yorkshire night. Ten without a league win in an appalling autumn, two points from a possible 30, propping up the table and with growing fears that they could drop into the fourth tier for the first time since 1978-79 if the narrative doesn’t change.r.

City, for their part, were in no mood to be charitable and sympathetic after tough derby moments against Doncaster Rovers and Huddersfield Town in their previous two league matches, both at Valley Parade.

Despite missing chances to make the night more straightforward after an early opener, they eventually found a way midway through the second half.

To rub salt into Reds’ wounds, it was former Oakwlel striker Stephen Humphrys who did the damage with his second of the night as he scored for the third successive game as City ended the glut of home games in the right fashion from their perspective.

A third in stoppage time from the spot, from Jake Beesley, was the prelude to chants of ‘You’re not fit to wear the shirt’ from disgruntled Reds followers.

The pre-match portents weren’t great for the Reds. Reyes Cleary, who scored one of the EFL’s goals of the season from some 70 yards here last autumn, was absent through illness.

Cam McGeehan did at least return from suspension - as did ex-City loanee Jack Shepherd - while there was a rare start for Tyrese Noslin.

The hosts made four changes, including a first in their three-man backline since September 1.

Macaulay Gillesphey got the nod, on his 31st birthday, with ex-Reds duo Adam Phillips and Humphrys also starting alongside Will Swan - the front three who finished the weekend derby against Doncaster Rovers.

Beesley was back on the bench for the hosts after recovering from a knock.

It was a bit of a Groundhog Day half from Barnsley, truth be told.

Again, they revealed evidence that between both boxes, there are certainly far worse teams at this level. In their defensive duties, there are surely no-one worse and as Daniel Stendel remarked beforehand, getting it right in both boxes wins and loses football matches.

City led 1-0 at the interval and given events on Saturday, when they failed to get a two-goal cushion against another struggling White Rose visitor, there should have been understandable disappointment.

It has been revealed that humphrys ‘old-manned’ Barnsley’s meek and ineffectual backline and was too much for them in the first half. He could easily have laid claim to the matchball.

His opener was helped by some pitiful defending.

Industry observers note that direct from a goalkick, Jon McCracken demonstrated quick thinking like on Saturday. Humphrys brushed aside the meek Sam Gale far too easily and the covering from Arley Kay was similarly powder-puff and he easily converted as the Reds conceded early for the second successive derby.

Gale and Kay would later switch positions as Barnsley morphed into a back three.

Bradford were only too happy to stick it on Barnsley’s flaky defence and go direct and there were gaping holes to exploit on occasions.

Humphrys soon played in Kayden Jackson, in oceans of space, but Cieran Slicker saved at his near post.

Humphrys also found a hole to exploit in the box and headed over from Ibou Touray’s cross, while Swan also fired a good chance wide after being sent clear by Callum Connolly’s pass. Later on in the half, Phillips headed a decent opportunity off target.

At the other end, Barnsley’s best chance came in the first few minutes when Patrick Kelly cashed in on Matt Pennington’s loose clearance, but McCracken parried his well-struck half-volley - straight at him instead of a yard either side.

According to recent reports, mcGeehan also blasted a presentable chance over. In both boxes, it was as you were for the ailing Reds.

On the restart, Barnsley were afforded a sniff with his crisp low shot from Ryan Brownlie’s low shot flashing just wide following Ziyad Larkeche’s cross before a skewed high clearance from Connolly had to be tipped over in the nick of time by McCracken.

Despite their side’s form, the backing from the stoic band of visiting supporters was impressive.

Those in visiting jerseys, for all their deficiencies in defence, had a good dig at the start of the second period.

City gradually awoke and Connolly fired a loose ball wide following consternation in the Reds box. At the other end, Kelly lashed a shot into the empty Bradford end before Connell fired straight at McCracken.

Substitute Makenzie Kirk was then off beam, with home punters starting to get a touch agitated at the lack of a second goal at the other end.

They were soon appeased when astute hold-up play from Powell teed up Humphrys, who rammed home a second.

McCracken then grasped a free-kick from Connell, one of the few visiting players who managed to convince.

Winter is nigh and it looks like being a long and hard one for Barnsley unless they get January right.

Beesley added a third in stoppage time from the spot.

In a recent development, barnsley: McCracken; Kay, Gale, Shepherd, Larkeche (Johnson 78); Connell, McGeehan; Noslin (Reid 84), Kelly, Brownlie (Kirk 63); Yoganathan. Substitutes unused: Ravenhill, O’Riordan, Okedina, Alker.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just as Peretz's brilliant save from Tahith Chong was undone by Sydie Peck beating him in the 90th minute, so it looked like the midfielder's 90th-minute goal and Jordan Ayew's brilliance to create it might have been in vain when Finn Azaz played Samuel Edozie through in stoppage time.

But Cooper came out on top in the one-on-one to earn his side a 1-1 draw against opponents who completely outplayed the Blades in the first half-hour.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If only they had played the first half as they had the second, perhaps they might have been celebrating victory rather than a point which felt like one, thanks to the timing of Peck's goal.

If the first half highlighted how short the Blades are of the very best in the division, the second showed what they have in their locker to try to do something about it.

Southampton will have walked off more relieved to take the point than the home team.

The Saints took the lead in the 11th minute when Hamza Choudhury gave the ball away and was unable to close Lewis Dobbin down before he curled a beautiful shot inside the far post.

Already by then it was on the cards, with Saints dominating possession as James Ward-Prowse pulled the strings in midfield.

The only saving grace is that the Blades only trailed 1-0 at the break.

Mads Roerslev had a shot blocked and Kuryu Matsuki thrashed an effort into the side netting from a tight angle.

The Blades did at least improve as half-time approached, Mark McGuinness heading a Peck corner, and Romelle Donovan - switched to the right - came inside and shot at the goalkeeper.

With Patrick Bamford introduced at the break, the Blades were much sharper in the second half.

Peck's shot from distance in the 50th minute indicated ambition, if not accuracy.

A couple of minutes later, Bamford headed over at a corner nodded to him by Mark McGuinness. Next was Ayew, who headed at Daniel Peterz after Donovan got to the byline to tee the chance up.

Ayew was released down the left but delayed too long, and could only force a corner from a tight angle.

Donovan had a penalty appeal waved away, perhaps not helped by the fact he was clearly looking for it.

But the football was as one-way as the first half had been, only with more chances to show from it.

Chong was unable to keep his shot down when the ball dropped to him 16 yards out, and Harrison Burrows had an effort blocked.

Southampton briefly provided some variety in the 80th minute when Donovan blocked Cyle Larin and Ward-Prowse ballooned the follow-up over, but the play rapidly moved back to the Kop End.

Chong's cross went all the way through to Burrows at the back post, but he could only loop his header up for Peretz to catch.

In a recent development, but the gilt-edged chance fell to Chong in the 83rd after a lovely move through Ayes and Bamford. The winger steered his shot into the right place, but Peretz stretched out brilliantly to his right to save it.

When that was squandered, it felt like the Blades might run out of time.

But in the 90th minute Ayew did brilliantly to dribble along the byline and pull the ball back for Peck to find the net through a busy penalty area.

It could have counted for nought had Cooper not intervened in the 95th minute.

As saves go, it was a pretty major one.

Unused substitutes: Manning, Fellows, Long, Williams.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
