📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he stated, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

Sources indicate that 🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, it should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he mentioned. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

Sources indicate that he added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

Latest Update: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1170 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • In a recent development, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

In a recent development, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

The plate and the photos are on show at the upcoming exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, indicates exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Sources indicate that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of vital artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

Recent findings suggest that however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

The dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked substantial and dangerous.".

Sources indicate that the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian indicates. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a new image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

The designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

In a recent development, still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

But altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

According to recent reports, the feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

In a recent development, "It's really crazy," she indicates, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

How to make AI data centres more sustainable

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1332 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M.
  • Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • Recent findings suggest that people have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

Around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Recent findings suggest that people have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

Future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

In a recent development, the Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres currently consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency states.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

There are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

But none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that new energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

Many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of newly introduced energy needed to power data centres.

In a recent development, how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

It has been revealed that how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

It has been revealed that one solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any upcoming generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

There is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a initiative for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI declared what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the company can work around peaks in power demand.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Sources indicate that these are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any latest energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

Sources indicate that there are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

Industry observers note that it felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

Industry observers note that in the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

In a recent development, there was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k.

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Sources indicate that instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

It has been revealed that they are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

Erling Haaland gives Manchester City the lead against Liverpool 🎯 https://t.co/cELo5y60Fk.

In fact, Liverpool’s best performers were the young attackers Victor Muñoz and, making his first league start as a makeshift centre-forward, Lewis Koumas, who is just 21. Against that, City unleashed a battery of forward talent.

"Koumas & Munoz were better than the two £100million players!" Jamie Carragher is still disappointed with what he's seeing from Florian Wirtz in a Liverpool shirt 😬🔴 https://t.co/jJwOZbPJ4b.

Was it an unfair advantage? It appears City have been thriving off that for some time and, while this team were not signed during the years the club have been found guilty of cheating, the argument is, of course, that they would not have joined without the sporting supremacy.

Recent findings suggest that certainly not Haaland, despite his avowed love for City. That cannot be doubted as his father, Alf-Inge, a former midfielder for the club, stood celebrating in the away end. The striker missed one chance when he should have scored, sent through on goal, shaking his head in disbelief at getting his angles wrong. It felt like a warning and that went unheeded as Doku, who had replaced one of their substantial summer signings in Iliman Ndiaye, cut in from the left with his shot deflecting into Haaland’s path. He made no mistake with a powerful, first-time finish.

Doku soon added a second, a sublime strike, as he dribbled goalwards, defenders backing off, and he arced a right-footed shot high beyond Alisson Becker’s grasp.

In a recent development, "It's a GEM" 💎 A beautiful strike from Jérémy Doku to double Man City's lead! https://t.co/lCUFfQmdLC.

Industry observers note that there were delighted chants of “olé” from the City supporters and that arrogance was rewarded by a strutting, emphatic third goal. It was finished by the mercurial Rayan Cherki after he was sent clear by a backheel from Josko Gvardiol, another substitute.

A moment of individual brilliance from Rayan Cherki to put the game beyond all doubt 🤯 https://t.co/wvmTMZcGhW.

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. In a sea of uncertainty as to what will now happen, that is something we can be sure of.

According to recent reports, “Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, noted. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

In a recent development, “Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”.

Maresca remarked City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”.

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca remarked. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”.

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

In a recent development, given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to return to winning ways in the Champions League when they continue their league stage campaign against Viking FK on Wednesday night.

This match will represent the first-ever contest between Atletico and Viking, although the Spanish team have won six of their seven previous meetings against Norwegian clubs.

Atletico boast a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's Champions League league stage, with the result leaving them 23rd in the overall table on four points.

Diego Simeone's side opened their league stage campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Liverpool before beating Manchester United and then drawing with Stuttgart, but they suffered a 2-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich in their last fixture in the competition.

The Red and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight, with the result leaving them third in the La Liga table on 31 points, five points behind leaders Barcelona.

Atletico lost 2-1 on aggregate to Arsenal in last season's Champions League semi-finals, and they have been runners-up in this tournament on two occasions (2014 and 2016).

Viking, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's league stage, and they actually sit above Atletico in the table (22nd).

The Eliteserien champions lost their section opener to Stuttgart before claiming a point in a 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich, but they were then beaten by Aston Villa at Villa Park.

The Dark Blues did have a huge European win last time out, though, recording a 4-1 victory over Sabah, which gave their hopes of qualification a huge boost.

Viking, who are jointly-managed by Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen, are playing in the Champions League for the first time since 1992-93, when they were beaten by Barcelona in the first round.

Latest Update: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1054 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • Recent findings suggest that "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • Industry observers note that the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

Recent findings suggest that "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

Industry observers note that the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Industry observers note that names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

"A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

According to recent reports, but a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, highlights how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

Sources indicate that names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer noted their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

Research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

Sources indicate that "Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

Industry observers note that even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

Pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

Sources indicate that "People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

Sources indicate that later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she said.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

But the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

"I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

But Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum said.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

That does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

In a recent development, online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

It has been revealed that pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Gerrard fears Mauricio Pochettino is already on collision course with one of his senior Manchester United players following Sunday’s damaging 4-0 defeat against Liverpool.

Any hope of a newly introduced manager bounce was extinguished during a frantic opening quarter of an hour at Anfield yesterday when the hosts roared into a two goal lead following Leny Yoro’s sending off.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled on the agony in the closing stages and ensured the scoreline gave a more accurate representation of Liverpool’s near total dominance.

While playing the entire match at a numerical disadvantage certainly played a role in the one-sided nature of such an eagerly anticipated contest, United were second best from the off and were made to pay for their fresh manager’s questionable team selection.

The decision to drop Harry Maguire at the expense of Matthijs de Ligt, who is still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was questioned by the likes of Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville before kick-off and their skepticism was vindicated when the Dutch centre-half played a role in Yoro’s red card.

Gerrard, meanwhile, went a step further in his criticism by accusing Pochettino of showing a lack of respect to Maguire by relegating him to the bench in his first game at the helm.

It has been revealed that ‘I thought he got it wrong,’ Gerrard told The Overlap with Sky Bet. ‘I thought he got it wrong in the back line. I think to start someone in a game of that magnitude, it’s the biggest game in the country. All eyes are on it all over the world.

‘To play someone that hadn’t played since last November. You can understand the manager wanting to come in and put his stamp on it and change a few things that had been going on previously, but Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment.

According to recent reports, ‘Forget the youngsters that are maybe not ready at the moment. Matthijs de Ligt’s been out for a year. Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It has been revealed that ‘And he made a difference when he came on. And he was one who was putting his body on the line. He made a great block, I think it was around the 38th, 39th minute, which stopped a certain goal. And I’ve watched Manchester United a lot this season, and he’s one who’s having a go.

‘He’s one who is rolling his sleeves up and having a go. Okay, he hasn’t been perfect, but to not play him and put de Ligt in before him, I thought it was a bit disrespectful.’.

Pochettino and United will have to soldier on with what they have until January when the transfer window reopens and strengthening a defence which is now official the worst in Europe’s top five leagues will represent a priority.

Gerrard added: ‘It’s just who’s available and who wants to sell and let good players go at the moment, so they’re going to have to pay big money.

‘There’s going to be a tax with that, because if United want to go and take, they need world-class centre-halves in January, cause waiting until the summer might be too late, so they need world-class centre-halves.

‘Who’s going to let world-class centre-halves go in January? Unless someone’s prepared to pay astronomical money. That’s what’s going to have to happen.’.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026.

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'.

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr.

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child.

'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most notable thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

'(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more key in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'.

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

  • The fixture was moved from October 31 because of Hibernian's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and both clubs arrive after heavy defeats on November 21, with Hibernian beaten 4-0 at home by Dundee United and Dundee thrashed 8-0 by Heart of Midlothian at Dens Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 23 Nov 2026 19:39, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 19:39.

Hibernian FC host Dundee FC in the Scottish Premiership at Easter Road Stadium on Tuesday.

The fixture was moved from October 31 because of Hibernian's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and both clubs arrive after heavy defeats on November 21, with Hibernian beaten 4-0 at home by Dundee United and Dundee thrashed 8-0 by Heart of Midlothian at Dens Park.

Marink Reedijk's Hibernian sit 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 11 points from 13 games, a return of three wins, two draws and eight defeats, and their goal difference of minus six is the product of 15 goals scored and 21 conceded.

The Hibees are the only club in the division yet to win a league match at home this season, and they have conceded 15 goals in seven league games at Easter Road.

Dundee United made that record worse on Saturday, with Zac Sapsford scoring from the rebound after Raphael Sallinger saved his sixth-minute penalty, adding a second before half time, and Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall completing a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's heaviest home defeat to United.

Reedijk was appointed on September 24 after David Gray was sacked, and he lost his first three league games in charge, 1-0 at Dundee United on October 10 and 2-1 at home to both Falkirk on October 17 and Celtic on October 25.

The cup has been kinder, as goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath beat Heart of Midlothian 2-1 at Hampden Park on November 1, Hibernian's first win over their city rivals at the national stadium after four defeats there, and set up a Premier Sports Cup final against Rangers on Sunday, December 13.

McGrath then struck a 25-yard shot just before the hour at Pittodrie on November 7, and substitutes Callum Wright, Nicky Cadden and Thibault Klidje added the rest in a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's biggest at Aberdeen since 1968 and remains Reedijk's only league victory.

Joe Newell, who wore the captain's armband against United in place of the injured Felix Passlack, spoke afterwards of the players' shame and embarrassment, and the midfielder will know that Tuesday offers the first chance to answer it in front of the Easter Road crowd.

Steven Pressley's Dundee sit seventh with 17 points from 13 games, a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats that leaves them six points and four places above Hibernian, with 18 goals scored and 23 conceded.

The Dee had conceded only 15 times in their first 12 league games and collected five wins in that run, with Owen Goodman playing every minute in goal and keeping two clean sheets.

That solidity vanished on Saturday, when Hearts led 4-0 at half time and Owen Bevan was sent off on 56 minutes for a foul on Claudio Braga, with the visitors winning 8-0 in what The Courier described as Dundee's worst-ever defeat at Dens Park.

Pressley took responsibility for the display afterwards, while pundit Richard Foster argued the players must also own a result that was Hearts' biggest top-flight win since 1957.

The defeat came a fortnight after a 2-1 loss at St Johnstone on November 7, and it ended an unbeaten home run of four league games for a side that had collected the bulk of its points at Dens Park.

Dundee will also remember that Hibernian won the first meeting 2-1 at Dens Park on August 30, and Tuesday is the second of three league games between the sides before the split.

Bradley Fink and Joe Westley share the Dundee scoring lead with four league goals each, and Westley, who takes the penalties, came off the bench to equalise at St Johnstone within two minutes of the restart.

Passlack, who took the captaincy from Boyle after Reedijk's arrival, is out with a hamstring injury sustained in the eighth minute at Aberdeen, and Reedijk has refused to put a date on his return as the defender races to be fit for the Rangers final.

Alex Williams replaced Passlack at Pittodrie and made his first start against United, so he is the likely right-back again.

Grant Hanley is out after thumb surgery, Adam Mayor has a hamstring problem, and on-loan Stoke City striker Nathan Lowe has a stress fracture that Reedijk will assess week by week.

Kanayo Megwa remains sidelined with a thigh problem and Rocky Bushiri is still recovering from the Achilles injury he suffered in May.

Left-back Jordan Obita is back in contention after a calf injury, and on-loan Manchester United midfielder Jacob Devaney returned from international duty with Ireland, giving Reedijk extra options if he rings the changes.

Owen Elding, 20, leads the line in Lowe's absence, with Boyle and McGrath operating around him as they did in the Hampden semi-final.

For the visitors, Bevan serves the first of a two-match ban after his straight red card against Hearts, ruling him out at Easter Road and at Aberdeen on Saturday, November 28.

Joe Wright, who was on the bench against Hearts, is the natural replacement alongside Ryan Astley, but he has played little league football this season.

Simon Murray, Finlay Robertson and Jack Moorhouse are all out for the season with anterior cruciate ligament injuries.

Bobby Wales, the on-loan striker, is still recovering from an ankle injury.

Goodman, beaten eight times at Dens Park, is expected to keep his place in goal.

Hibernian possible starting lineup:.

Sallinger; Williams, Kerr, Ivezic, Iredale; Chaiwa, Newell; McGrath, Mulligan, Boyle; Elding.

Dundee possible starting lineup:.

Sources indicate that goodman; D. Wright, Astley, J. Wright, Samuels; Forrest, Hamilton, Finnigan, Reilly; Westley, Fink.

Hibernian have not won a league game at Easter Road all season and have shipped 15 goals in seven home matches, and a side that has just lost 4-0 to United at home is unlikely to turn that around in three days against opponents who beat them at Dens Park on August 30.

Dundee arrive without Bevan and with the memory of an 8-0 defeat, and a makeshift centre-back pairing facing Elding and Boyle will struggle to hold a clean sheet.

The counter-argument is that Pittodrie remains Reedijk's only league win, but Dundee's points have come overwhelmingly at Dens Park, and their goal difference of minus five is the worst in the top eight, which is why a Hibernian goal looks likelier than a clean sheet for either side.

United opted against signing a new forward in the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired given the setbacks encountered by Benjamin Sesko.

The Slovenia international displayed signs of promise after a difficult start to his United career last season following his £74million move from RB Leipzig.

A nagging shin injury has restricted the 23-year-old to just six appearances so far this term and he is unlikely to return until the New Year at the earliest.

Manchester United fans should not expect much transfer business to be done this winter, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to be given a meagre budget to work with in January.

The Argentine has arrived as the new Red Devils boss and took charge of his first game on Sunday, which did not go well at all as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win over their old rivals at Anfield.

Leny Yoro was shown an early red card, leaving Pochettino’s prepares in tatters as defeat left Manchester United 19th in the Premier League table.

With just one win and 23 goals conceded in 11 league outings, there have been calls for signings to be made, especially in defence.

Before Pochettino was appointed, club legend Gary Neville even urged him to turn down the job unless the hierarchy promised to sign two defenders over the winter transfer window.

That may still happen, but it will have to be some canny business as the Daily Mail reports that Manchester United will have ‘well under £50 million’ to spend in the next transfer window.

Having focused on midfield signings over the summer, United want a centre-back, left-back and striker, but obviously that cannot be done to any level of quality on such a meagre budget.

Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins has been touted as a target, but the 25-year-old would not be a cheap option.

The Bees paid £23m for him when they signed him from Wolves three years ago and he remains under contract until 2029.

The Republic of Ireland international has been a mainstay in the team since moving to Brentford, although is presently out with injury.

Summer targets at left-back included Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri and Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, both of whom could be options again.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been linked with a move to Old Trafford, having worked with Pochettino in his stint as USA manager.

The former Arsenal man came close to joining Everton in a £40m deal over the summer before the deal collapsing at the last minute.

Manchester United may look to make a loan signing to keep costs down, although could stretch the budget if they feel that relegation is a genuine threat.

Industry observers note that neville does not think it will come to a relegation scrap, despite United’s woeful form, saying after the defeat to Liverpool: ‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight. They’re second-bottom in the league, it’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years. I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.

However, he added: ‘You could arrogantly look at Coventry at home, or Sunderland at home, and think United will be alright. But the performance levels we’re seeing at the moment don’t give you much confidence.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Piers Morgan has accused Cole Palmer of wasting his talent and displaying a rotten attitude following his refusal to acknowledge Chelsea’s fans following Saturday’s defeat against Leeds United.

The Stamford Bridge faithful could hardly believe what they were witnessing as Daniel Farke’s side romped to a 4-1 win that represented their first victory in west London since 1999.

Palmer delivered another anonymous performance and has registered just one goal contribution in his last five matches, a penalty in a 2-0 win over Manchester United earlier this month.

To compound another lackluster display, the former Manchester City forward refused to clap the home fans and became involved in an altercation with teammate Joao Pedro before he trudged down the tunnel.

With Thomas Tuchel steadfastly refusing to find space for Palmer in his England squad, the 24-year-old’s career is in danger of fizzling out unless he knuckles down, according to Morgan.

He told Sports Uncensored: “I’m sorry, but he’s a massive d***head. The guy, on and off the pitch, is a d***head.

‘The way he refused to go over to the fans. The way he treats the fans in the street.

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

Sources indicate that asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole mentioned of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

In a recent development, ‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve noted it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

According to recent reports, ‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

It has been revealed that ‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .

"Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

The ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells. Existing operations must be phased out within city limits over the next 20 years.

Though LA City is only part of greater Los Angeles, the move affects hundreds of active wells and thousands of inactive ones, many located in working class communities of color.

It has been revealed that "In South LA, working-class families have had corporations drilling across the street from their homes," stated council president Marqueece Harris-Dawson in a statement. "No one should have to live near an oil drilling site.".

Rock Zierman, CEO of the California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA), told DW, "CIPA believes this ordinance constitutes an unlawful taking of private property.".

LA follows much smaller Culver City, also in California, in moving against urban oil production, and begins the process of ending its long, complex relationship with fossil fuels.

California's oil industry expanded rapidly in the early 20th century, when the state produced roughly a quarter of the world's oil. Lots of that so-called black gold was around LA and as the city grew, homes, schools and businesses were built around existing oil infrastructure.

Today, wells can be found beneath residential areas, close to playgrounds, along the coast and in some of the city's most densely populated and largely working-class neighborhoods. Some have been permanently sealed or plugged for decades, while others remain active or are idle.

Under California law, an idle well is one that has not produced oil for two years. Unlike plugged wells, they can potentially return to production.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Residents living near the active and inactive wells report strong odors, headaches, nausea and breathing difficulties. Another concern is air quality. Oil wells can release toxic pollutants, including benzene and hydrogen sulfide, and research has linked proximity to oil extraction with higher rates of respiratory illness and reduced lung function.

But both active and idle wells can also leak methane — a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change — while residents say occasional accidents or breakages send oil flowing down city streets.

"Frontline communities have been experiencing or have experienced for decades living near these toxic sites and having to pay for that with their health," stated Miranda, a policy director with Esperanza Community Housing, a nonprofit providing affordable housing services.

Industry observers note that miranda told DW she and her mother both have asthma. The council vote "definitely represents hope," she added.

LA City Council initially approved an ordinance to phase out oil extraction back in 2022 after successful lobbying by residents like Wendy Miranda. But oil companies challenged the measure in court, with industry groups successfully arguing that the city lacked the legal authority to impose the ban.

California subsequently passed legislation giving local governments greater power to regulate and restrict oil and gas operations, putting the possibility of a phaseout back on the table.

In an emailed statement to DW, CIPA CEO Rock Zierman remarked energy companies were prepared to challenge the newly introduced ordinance.

Zierman added that it would make city residents more dependent on foreign oil from countries with lower environmental standards when they are "already struggling" with high gas prices.

"It sends the jobs, investment and revenue elsewhere while leaving Californians to pay the bill," stated Zierman.

Industry observers note that the relationship between local oil production and prices at the pump is not straightforward and is influenced by a number of factors, according to the California Energy Commission, the state's main energy policy agency. Those include the cost of crude oil, refining, transportation, distribution and local taxes.

Even though the US is the world's largest oil producer, it exports and imports crude oil, as well as refined petroleum products. Because oil is traded globally, US residents are exposed to the same price fluctuations as people elsewhere, no matter how much of the fossil fuel is produced domestically.

Recent findings suggest that california's oil industry and the amount of oil it produces have been steadily declining since the 1980s. In the coastal lowlands known as the LA Basin, output is 43% lower than eight years ago, with the amount of oil extracted falling more rapidly than the number of open wells.

In a recent development, when wells stop producing, it is up to the oil operators to remove equipment and plug them. The state agency that regulates oil and gas, CalGEM, and the LA fire department oversee plugging operations, and also seal wells for which no-one takes responsibility.

But many have not yet been plugged — some 80% of idle wells in LA have been inactive for more than eight years, and about a third for over a century.

Industry observers note that the cost of plugging a well also varies widely, with estimates ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. California law requires operators to submit plugging plans or face annual fines that increase with the amount of time the well has been idle.

But those fines aren't always paid. According to CalGEM's own data, the agency collected just $1 million out of $36 million (€32 million) in fines in 2025.

Industry observers note that A report by Carbon Tracker also found that if all future profits from oil companies operating in California went to decommissioning wells, the state would still face a shortfall of $7 billion. The cost would by default fall to taxpayers, according to Carbon Tracker.

Miranda told DW that the next step for community activists is to reduce the 20-year timeline and have the oil sector "pay for this cleanup."  For now, she is claims both she and her mother are hopeful that future generations "can have better health and breathe cleaner air.".

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are said to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

Recent findings suggest that ‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

Sources indicate that ‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

Nicky Butt believes that Liverpool will prove to be Arsenal’s main title challengers over the likes of Manchester City this season.

Defending champions Arsenal extended their lead at the top of the table to six points after a hard-fought draw away at Newcastle.

Brighton had the chance to cut that lead to just three points, but a late Oli McBurnie brace saw them lose 2-0 to Hull City on Sunday.

Manchester City did snap their three-match losing streak, but a 1-1 draw on Fulham means Enzo Maresca’s side are now winless in four Premier League matches and also six points off the league leaders.

City will have the opportunity to eat into Arsenal’s lead at the top of the table when the two sides meet at the Emirates next week.

However, Butt does not expect them to last the course in this season’s title race, instead talking up Liverpool’s chances after their impressive 4-0 win over Manchester United on Sunday.

‘Any win for Liverpool against Man United or vice versa is massive,’ Butt said on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.

It has been revealed that ‘Forget the ten men or the level of the team they are playing against at the time. When Liverpool beat Man United or the other way around, it’s a massive result, especially for a new manager.

‘It was only a couple of years ago that they won the league, so they’re not a bad team, and they’ve added well.

‘And they haven’t half spent a few quid, they’ve got three £100m-plus players so you would expect them to be alright.’.

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that it was crucial that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team indicated the levels that they are capable of.

Sources indicate that now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

It has been revealed that “It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it revealed towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

Sources indicate that “We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

Sources indicate that “I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

“I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

Sources indicate that “The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

Industry observers note that “But that’s not an excuse. I said the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

Recent findings suggest that “Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

“Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an important objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

“I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

“Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.
